metadata.title: Claude, Deal Team Summary.
metadata.purpose: Redo of the claude-for-legal reel in the hai-simple form: a hesitant-writer cold open, Plain register, Liam narrating, Humanitarians AI outro. Source facts kept where the source sheet actually had them (a skill is a folder Claude reads before acting; SKILL.md is the instruction set; steps run in order; reliability is repeatable structure, not judgment). The source's task-specific fields were unfilled template placeholders (literal '>' characters) and its SKILL.md path is unreachable from this machine; the one task-specific fact used here (a deal-team status summary: parties, key terms, status, open issues, next steps) is inferred directly from the skill's own name, not fabricated detail.
metadata.clock: narration (Kokoro am_onyx) — master clock; conform each beat to measured audio
metadata.prerequisites: none — general audience, no legal or technical background assumed
metadata.exclusions: the exact contents of the real deal-team-summary SKILL.md (unreachable from this build — see SCRIPT.md source-fidelity note); legal advice; document types beyond a term sheet and an NDA
metadata.anchor_pair: S06 -> S07 (Aster Corp / Vale Robotics, same illustrative case)

beats.narration_text: You might think Claude writes a deal team summary by magic — like it just knows. It doesn't: it follows instructions, in a file called a skill. Here's what's inside it.

props.text:
Claude writes a deal
team summary by
magic?

beats.narration_text: A merger is underway. Lawyers, bankers, and executives all need the same picture: parties, key terms, status, open issues, next steps. Ask five people for that update and you get five different shapes.

items.label: Parties, terms, status, issues, next steps
items.sub: A merger needs one shared picture: parties, key terms, status, open issues, next steps.

items.label: Ask five people, get five shapes
items.sub: Ask five people for that update, and you get five different shapes for the same deal.

beats.narration_text: The natural assumption is that Claude already knows how to shape this — good judgment, no separate instructions required. It's read enough deal documents to just handle it.

items.label: Claude already knows how to shape this
items.sub: The natural assumption: good judgment, no separate instructions required.

items.label: It's read plenty of deals
items.sub: It's read enough deal documents before to just handle it.

beats.narration_text: Ask for the same deal's summary twice, with no skill installed, and the two answers don't match — different fields, different order, sometimes a missing item. Judgment alone isn't repeatable.

items.label: Same deal, asked twice, no skill
items.sub: Ask for the same deal's summary twice, with no skill installed.

items.label: Different fields, different order, missing items
items.sub: The two answers don't match — different fields, different order, sometimes a missing item.

beats.narration_text: A skill fixes that. It's a folder Claude reads before it acts — this one called deal-team-summary. Inside is one file, SKILL.md, plain language, no hidden logic. The file is the instructions.

items.label: deal-team-summary: one file, SKILL.md
items.sub: A skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts — this one called deal-team-summary.

items.label: Plain language, no hidden logic
items.sub: Inside is one file, SKILL.md — plain language. The file is the instructions.

beats.narration_text: Inside SKILL.md is a list of steps. Claude reads them in order and runs each one — pull the parties, pull the terms, check status, flag open issues, list next steps. Linear, no shortcuts.

items.label: Parties → terms → status → issues → next steps
items.sub: Claude reads the steps in SKILL.md and runs each one in order.

items.label: Linear. No shortcuts.
items.sub: No branching unless the file itself says so.

beats.narration_text: Take one illustrative deal: Aster Corp buying Vale Robotics. Feed the skill the term sheet, the disclosure schedule, and the latest redline. Same five fields come back — parties, terms, status, open issues, next steps.

items.label: Term sheet, disclosure schedule, redline
items.sub: One illustrative deal: Aster Corp buying Vale Robotics. Feed the skill the source documents.

items.label: Same five fields, every time
items.sub: Parties, terms, status, open issues, next steps — the same shape comes back.

beats.narration_text: Run it again next week, after the redline changes. The five fields are still there, same order — only the contents update. That's what a skill buys: the shape holds, the deal moves.

items.label: Same deal, one week later
items.sub: Run it again after the redline changes.

items.label: Same five fields, same order
items.sub: Only the contents update — the shape holds, the deal moves.

beats.narration_text: A consistent shape doesn't prove the deal is healthy — the skill structures whatever the documents say, including a bad clause or a stale draft. Structure isn't a check on the underlying facts.

items.label: A consistent shape isn't a healthy deal
items.sub: The skill structures whatever the documents say — good or bad.

items.label: Including a bad clause or a stale draft
items.sub: Structure isn't a check on the underlying facts.

beats.narration_text: And two summaries that look different without the skill aren't necessarily wrong — they might both be reasonable readings, just organized differently. That's the exact inconsistency the skill removes.

items.label: Two summaries, no skill, both look different
items.sub: They aren't necessarily wrong — just organized differently.

items.label: That's the inconsistency the skill removes
items.sub: Same input, same structure, every single run.

beats.narration_text: A skill doesn't make Claude better at judgment. It makes Claude follow the same steps, in the same order, every single time.

props.quote: A skill doesn't make Claude better at judgment. It makes Claude follow the same steps, in the same order, every single time.
props.sparkLine: Same steps. Same order. Every time.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Here's the prompt — read it with me. I'm working a deal and have a term sheet and a signed NDA. Summarize this deal for the deal team — but tell me your structure first, before you fill it in. Then run it again from scratch, and tell me if the structure changed.

props.command: I'm working a deal and have a term sheet and a signed NDA. Summarize this deal for the deal team — but first tell me the exact structure you'll use (the fields, and their order) before you fill anything in. Then run the same summary again from scratch, and tell me if the structure changed.
